title: A Google Calendar event claims a milestone shipped, but it's still open
author: kwaku-ananse
description: The hundred-fifth real recipe, the thirteenth leg of the claims-open-milestone family (after commit, issue-body, issue-comment, linear-comment, mention, milestone, readme, release, review-comment, slack-message, tweet, and email), and the fourth leg the google_calendar+github toolkit's own claims-X grid has grown (after calendar-event-claims-unfixed-issue, calendar-event-claims-unmerged-pr, and calendar-event-claims-dangling-milestone -- the recipe that hundred-fourth recipe's own README named by name as a future recipe's own open seam). Extracts every 'milestone #N' claim phrase (the shared seam_engine.milestone_claims grammar every sibling already imports) from a calendar event's own title+description and checks whether the named milestone is still open. A claimed milestone that does not exist at all is excluded here -- that is calendar-event-claims-dangling-milestone's own seam, not this one's; a claimed milestone that is closed is excluded too, the claim was simply true. Fixture-only, MOCK ONLY, never a live network call -- zero Google Calendar tools are exposed on the-hand gateway today, same WIP note every Calendar recipe already carries. Neither scope is new (ListMilestones sat on the oath table from founding; ListEvents has sat on the Google Calendar row since milestone-deadline-no-calendar-event) and google_calendar+github is not a new toolkit pair.
confidence_notes: Age-gated 0.85/0.5 bar, keyed off the event's own start time -- holds calendar-event-claims-unfixed-issue's and email-claims-open-milestone's identical 24-hour bar exactly, not an independently re-reasoned number just because the claim targets a milestone instead of an issue or PR: an OPEN milestone could close at any moment, so a claim checked within 24 hours of the event's own start might just be a race the event hasn't caught up to yet, rather than a settled overclaim -- unlike calendar-event-claims-dangling-milestone's flat 0.8 (a nonexistent milestone number will never spontaneously start existing, so no grace period means anything there), an open milestone really could resolve at any moment, so the grace period means something here. A claimed milestone number that does not resolve to a real milestone at all is excluded at confidence 0.0 -- that is calendar-event-claims-dangling-milestone's own seam, not this one's. A claimed milestone that IS closed is excluded too, at confidence 0.0 -- the claim was simply true. An event with no 'milestone #N' claim phrase at all (a bare #N aside) produces no surfaced candidate. Fixture-only (source: "fixture") per SCOPES.md's own WIP note on the Google Calendar toolkit: zero Calendar-capable tools are exposed on the-hand gateway's live toolset today -- the detection logic is real, the live read waits on the Hand's gateway, and only the fixture loader swaps for a real call the day one appears.
